Add SortedList.add_left/add_right inherited correctly by SortedKeyList. add_left inserts before every equal comparison key (including across block boundaries); add_right preserves current add arrival order. Reuse cached-key/block/index bookkeeping, retain payload identity and key extraction semantics. Cover empty/natural/keyed/reverse-key containers, equal keys with unequal payloads, split/index invariants and subsequent bisect/deletion. Existing add remains unchanged; do not enable arbitrary unsorted insert.

Deliver real implementation, original-failing public tests at library/tests/test_development_sortedcontainers_01_dev.py, and Chinese compatibility documentation at library/docs/development-sortedcontainers-01-dev.md. Add SortedKeyList.refresh_at(index) with Python index protocol/negative indexes. A caller explicitly changed one payload key: remove by STORED index (never search with new key), rebuild a candidate index and reinsert at current key, then atomically commit only if all comparisons/key evaluations succeed. Return original payload identity. Other payload keys are required stable; a failed refresh preserves original stored ordering/key caches, without claiming rollback of caller object changes or key callback side effects. Maintain original key-stability default contract.

Deliver real implementation, original-failing public tests at library/tests/test_development_sortedcontainers_02_dev.py, and Chinese compatibility documentation at library/docs/development-sortedcontainers-02-dev.md. Add sorted_copy(key=None) to SortedList/SortedKeyList, SortedSet and SortedDict. Build a fully independent container of the same logical family using the selected key, preserving members/value identities and natural ordering for None. Original content/order/strategy never change, including when new key raises. Rebind all cached bisect/irange proxies to the new index; retain empty/copy/pickle behavior. SortedList factory may return keyed/unkeyed concrete list type; no subclass constructor guarantee or implicit in-place rekey.

Add floor/ceil/lower/higher(value,default=MISSING) to list/keyed list/set/dict. Use container bisect ordering: floor last <=, ceil first >=, lower strict predecessor, higher strict successor; keyed comparisons follow sorting key, including reverse keys and duplicate-key ties. Return existing value (dict returns key/value pair) preserving identity. Missing raises KeyError unless any explicit default, including None/False, is supplied. Existing indexing/bisect behavior unchanged.

Add pop_range(minimum=None,maximum=None,inclusive=(True,True),reverse=False) to all three sorted container families. Boundaries follow existing value/key bisect semantics, None is unbounded, inclusive flags explicit bool pair, reversed/empty interval no-op. Collect removed values (dict items) then use existing block/view slice deletion; preserve duplicates, object identity and all remaining indexes. reverse affects returned list only. Cover large cross-block windows, reverse keys and empty/full deletion; do not treat old view slicing as newly implemented capability.
